insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Restore Benefit Instant addition of 100% Basic Sum Insured on complete or partial utilization of Your existing Policy Sum Insured and Multiplier Benefit (if applicable) during the Policy Year.
great.reference: Section B, In-patient Benefits, 1.a Restore Benefit (page 14)
great.explanation: Provides an instant addition of 100% of the Basic Sum Insured when your existing Sum Insured (and Multiplier Benefit, if applicable) is partially or fully used in the same policy year. This increases your available cover for subsequent hospitalisations in that year.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as multiplier benefit irrespective of any claims
great.explanation: On renewal without a break, 50% of the Base Sum Insured is added as a multiplier benefit even if you made claims. This means your bonus does not get wiped out just because you claimed.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related treatment is not covered for the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Treatment for the listed conditions/surgeries is excluded until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common market-standard waiting period for specified illnesses.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered until 36 months of continuous coverage are completed. This is within the typical 2–4 year range seen in many plans.

good.name: Restore Benefit Limit
good.quote: i. The Sum Insured will be restored only once in a Policy Year. ii. If the Restored Sum Insured is not utilized in a Policy Year, it will expire.
good.reference: Section B, In-patient Benefits, 1.a Restore Benefit conditions (page 14)
good.explanation: The restored Sum Insured is available only once per policy year and any unused restored amount expires at the end of that year. This limits how many times you can rely on restore in a single year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalisation expenses... incurred upto 60 days before the date of admission
good.reference: Section B.1.b (page 11) and Schedule of Benefits (page 47-48)
good.explanation: Covers pre-hospitalisation medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalisation.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-Hospitalisation expenses... incurred upto 180 days after discharge from the Hospital
good.reference: Section B.1.c (page 11-12) and Schedule of Benefits (page 47-48)
good.explanation: Covers post-hospitalisation medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge. This supports longer recovery costs like follow-ups, diagnostics, and medicines.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: J(i) The amount payable in case of Air ambulance facility shall be either the actual expenses or Rs. 2.5 Lacs per hospitalisation, whichever is lower
good.reference: Section B.1.j (page 13) and Schedule of Benefits (page 47-48)
good.explanation: Pays for air ambulance charges up to the lower of actual expenses or ₹2.5 lakhs per hospitalisation. This can be valuable for emergency transfers but has a clear per-hospitalisation cap.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Annexure I List I - Items for which coverage is not available in the policy... 56 GLOVES... 60 MASK... 55 ECG ELECTRODES... 68 VASOFIX SAFETY
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, masks, ECG electrodes and similar items are listed as not covered. This can increase your out-of-pocket costs during hospitalisation even when the main bill is covered.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: Co-Payment (Optional benefit) I. If opted and mentioned on the Policy Schedule that a Co-payment is effective
bad.reference: Section B.2.d Co-Payment (Optional benefit) (page 15-16) and Schedule of Benefits (page 47-48)
bad.explanation: A co-payment can apply if you opt for it and it is shown as effective in the Policy Schedule. If selected, you will have to bear a part of each admissible claim, reducing the insurer payout.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.explanation: Room rent/boarding is included, but this clause does not state any room category limit or rupee cap. You should confirm the room rent eligibility in the Schedule of Benefits to avoid unexpected deductions.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
